# Starlark reader fixtures

Inputs for the unit tests of `socket_patch_core::bazel::starlark`
(`crates/socket-patch-core/src/bazel/starlark/mod.rs`). Nothing here was written by
socket-patch, and nothing here is built: no file has the name of a Bazel boundary file
(`MODULE.bazel`, `WORKSPACE`, `WORKSPACE.bazel`, `REPO.bazel`), so the directory is not a
Bazel workspace.

`.gitattributes` marks the directory `-text`. Line endings, a byte-order mark, a NUL and
bytes that are not UTF-8 are what several of these files test, and a conversion on checkout
would change them.

## `corpus/`: real files and the model they read to

Each file is a byte-for-byte copy of a file in a public repository at the tag given below
(for the Bazel Central Registry, at the commit given). `<name>.golden` beside it is the
statement model the reader produces, one statement per line with its line number; the test
`the_corpus_of_real_files_reads_to_its_goldens` compares them. After an intended change to
the reader, regenerate with

    SOCKET_PATCH_BLESS_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p socket-patch-core --lib bazel::starlark

and review the diff. The file name decides the dialect: `*MODULE.bazel` is a module file,
`*.WORKSPACE` a WORKSPACE file and `*.bzl` a macro file.

## `s5/`: what Bazel accepts

Probe S5 of the Bazel-support campaign ran 60 variants of one statement
(`V = <expr>` followed by `print("S5VAL", repr(V), len(V))`) through Bazel 5.4.1, 6.6.0,
7.7.2, 8.8.2, 9.3.2 and 10.0.0rc3, as a root `MODULE.bazel`, an included segment, a `.bzl`
file, a `BUILD` file and a `WORKSPACE`; 2026-11-11, one macOS arm64 machine. The driver, the
per-cell logs and the full table are in the campaign's probe directory
(`starlark-include/RESULTS.md` section 2.4), outside this repository.

- `module/<variant>`, `workspace/<variant>`: the byte-exact files the probe fed to Bazel.
- `bare/<variant>`: the vectors of the segment, `.bzl` and `BUILD` kinds, which are the same
  bytes (no `module()` or `workspace()` header). `tab-indent-def-body` exists for `.bzl` only.
- `accepts.tsv`: what Bazel did, one row per kind and variant: for each distinct outcome
  the versions that had it, then the printed `repr(V) len(V)` or `error`. Derived from the
  probe's `s5/accepts-<kind>-<version>.json`.
- `verdicts.golden`: what the reader does with each vector: `value "<text>" <len>`,
  `opaque` (the file is read and `V` has no value) or `refuse <kind>`.

The test `s5_verdicts_agree_with_what_bazel_accepts` holds the two together: a value must
be the one every Bazel printed, a refusal needs every Bazel to have rejected the file, and
everything else must be opaque.

The S1c rows of the same probe (`include()` syntax) are small enough to be written out in
the test `include_rows_of_probe_s1c` in `stmt.rs`.
